facts: Python is a high-level programming language known for clear, readable code.
The Python interpreter runs the instructions in a program in order, from top to bottom.
A variable is a name that refers to a value, such as age = 12.
print() shows a value as output.
In Python 3, dividing with / always gives a decimal number (a float), for example 240 / 3 gives 80.0.
CPython first compiles source code into bytecode, which its virtual machine then executes.
A generator uses yield to produce values one at a time instead of building a whole list in memory.

lesson.title: What is Python and how does it work?

scenes.heading: What is Python and how does it work?
scenes.subtitle: A clear language that a computer runs step by step

narration.text: Python is a programming language that uses simple, readable words.
You write instructions in a file that ends in dot p y.
The Python interpreter reads those instructions.
It runs them in order, from top to bottom.
Anything you print appears on the screen as output.
A variable is a name for a value. Here, name holds Asha.
Age holds the number twelve.
Print shows Hi and then the name, so we see Hi Asha.
Age plus one is thirteen, so the last line prints thirteen.
Most Python programs are built from four kinds of pieces.
Variables store values, and functions package steps you can reuse.
Lists and dictionaries hold many values together.
If statements and loops decide which steps run, and how often.

scenes.heading: Step 3: A function with a list

narration.text: Def creates a function called average that takes a list of marks.
It adds the marks and divides by how many there are.
Scores is a list of three numbers.
The total is two hundred forty, divided by three gives eighty point zero.
A common surprise: dividing with a slash always gives a decimal number.
The standard Python, called C Python, first compiles your source code into bytecode.
A virtual machine then executes the bytecode instructions one by one.
Every value is an object, and memory is freed when nothing refers to it any more.

scenes.heading: Step 5: Generators save memory

narration.text: Yield turns this function into a generator.
It produces one square at a time, only when asked, instead of storing a whole list.
Sum pulls the values zero, one, four and nine, which add up to fourteen.
The trade-off: a generator can only be read once, from start to end.

narration.text: Quick check. Why can a generator save memory?
It makes each value only when it is needed, so no full list is stored.
